name: 広島風お好み焼き くらわんか (Hiroshima-fu Okonomiyaki Kurawanka)

claims.text: Wheat is unavoidable here: okonomiyaki batter is wheat flour, the dish is built on wheat soba noodles, and it is cooked on a shared teppan griddle alongside other wheat-based okonomiyaki.
The okonomiyaki is finished with okonomiyaki/Worcestershire-style sauce, which conventionally contains wheat.

name: 廣島牡蠣 みやまえ (Hiroshima Kaki Miyamae)

claims.text: Dishes are seasoned in the standard Japanese izakaya style; soy-sauce-based seasonings contain wheat, and fried oysters (kaki fry) use a wheat batter/breading.

name: 広島かき酒場 MOMIJI (Hiroshima Kaki Sakaba MOMIJI)

claims.text: Dishes are seasoned in the standard Japanese izakaya manner with soy sauce, which normally contains wheat; no wheat-free seasoning is documented.

name: ひろしま丸かじり 中ちゃん (Hiroshima Marukajiri Naka-chan)

claims.text: A teppan (flat-grill) okonomiyaki and teppanyaki kitchen where wheat batter, wheat noodles and wheat-containing soy sauce are cooked on shared surfaces, making cross-contamination essentially unavoidable for gluten-sensitive diners.
Signature and everyday dishes (e.g. uni-cresson and teppanyaki items) are seasoned with soy sauce, which in Japan is standardly wheat-based.
The kitchen centers on seafood and meat (oysters, sea urchin, fish, pork, egg) cooked on the same teppan with butter, so animal-product contact is pervasive.

name: 広島名物 牡蠣一番 (Hiroshima Meibutsu Kaki Ichiban)

claims.text: Fried oysters, oyster gratin and okonomiyaki-style oysters use wheat flour/breading, and the fryer is also used for wheat-coated items, so cross-contact with gluten is likely throughout the menu.
Dishes are seasoned in the standard Japanese izakaya style with wheat-based soy sauce; no wheat-free soy sauce is documented.
Effectively every dish involves oysters, other seafood or fish-based dashi, so a fully plant-based meal is not realistic here.
An English-language menu is available, which makes it easier for travelers to identify ingredients before ordering.
